info.title: Hodor administration interface
info.description: Users, their sessions and second factors, the audit log, the identity providers, the keys, the applications, the assurance levels and the record of decisions of a tenant, for the people who run it. Paths are relative to https://{host}/t/{slug}/api/v1/admin. Every operation needs an access token whose user holds a role with the permission named in `x-hodor-permission`.

accessToken.description: An access token: `hodor_at_` followed by 64 hexadecimal characters.

authenticator_application.description: Null when the installation offers no authenticator application.

keys.description: Security keys and passkeys, oldest first.

second_factor_required.description: Whether the tenant requires a second factor.

code.description: A stable code for programs, for example `admin.forbidden`.

IdentityProvider.description: An identity provider of the tenant. It has no field for the client secret, which no operation returns.

alias.description: The provider's name in addresses. It never changes.

creates_users.description: Whether a person nobody knows yet is created on first sign-in.

callback_address.description: The address to register at the provider. `null` for a directory, which nobody leaves for.

trusts_email.description: Whether every address the provider gives is taken as vouched for, even when the provider does not say so.

directory.description: What only a directory has; `null` for every other kind.

saml.description: What only a SAML identity provider has; `null` for every other kind.

metadata_address.description: Hodor's metadata for a SAML identity provider, to give it; `null` for every other kind.

issuer.description: May be left out for the kind `github`.

client_id.description: Required for every kind but `saml`, which has none.

client_secret.description: Required for every kind but `saml`, which has none.

IdentityProviderChanges.description: What is left out stays as it is.

DirectoryInput.description: What is left out is `entryUUID`, `mail` and `cn` for the attribute names, or, in a change, what it was.

certificate.description: The identity provider's signing certificate, in PEM.

SamlInput.description: What is left out is `email` and `name` for the attribute names, or, in a change, what it was. A new provider needs the single sign-on address and the certificate.

KeyVersion.description: A key version, without anything of its key. Its `id` is the key identifier, `kid`, in the published key set.

first_party.description: A first-party application is not asked for consent.

consent_seconds.description: How long a person's consent to the client lasts before they are asked again.

id_token_signed_response_alg.description: How the client's ID tokens are signed. ES256 unless given.

secrets.description: The secrets that exist, never the secret or its hash.

jwk.description: The public key, as a JSON Web Key.

client_secret.description: The client's first secret, in this answer only, when it has a secret method. Hodor cannot show it again.

id_token_signed_response_alg.description: How the client's ID tokens are signed. ES256 unless given.
How the client's ID tokens are signed. ES256 unless given.

client_secret.description: The secret, in this answer only.

jwk.description: A public JSON Web Key with a `kid`; a key with a private part is refused.

audience.description: The audience of its tokens. Never changes.

acr.description: The name applications ask for in `acr_values` and tokens carry in `acr`.

application.description: The name of the client's application.

scopes.description: The scopes agreed to, never offline_access.

allow_sample_percent.description: The share of allows kept, with `sampled` and only then.

masks.description: Paths erased from the input before a record is stored: `subject.attributes.…`, `asserted.…`, `resource.attributes.…` or `context.attributes.…`, with `*` alone as the last segment.

input.description: What the engine was given, after the tenant's masks.
